memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the table of acacia wood - two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high. Then they overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold moulding around it. They also made round it a rim a handbreadth wide and put a gold moulding on the rim." - Exod 37:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A table. In the holy place, standing before God, there was a table for bread.

That is worth noticing. God did not fill His dwelling only with altars and instruments of sacrifice. He included a table — the most ordinary piece of furniture in any home, the place where families eat together.

Throughout Scripture, tables mean fellowship. To eat with someone is to accept them. That is why the religious leaders were scandalised that Jesus welcomed sinners and ate with them (Luke 15:2). It was too intimate.

Notice the rim around the edge — a handbreadth wide, with a gold moulding. A practical detail: it kept things from sliding off as the table travelled. God cares about the ordinary functioning of ordinary objects.

And this table points forward. Jesus took bread at a table and gave it to His friends (Luke 22:19). David sang that God prepares a table before us (Ps 23:5). And Scripture ends with an invitation to the wedding supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9).

Our God is not distant and formal. He sets a table.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of God as someone who welcomes you to a table?
2. Who do you eat with, and who might God want you to welcome?
3. How does the Lord's Supper shape your sense of belonging to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You set a table and invite me to it. Make me welcoming to others as You have been to me. Amen.
